risks: Text touches, text aliases and org are discovery/display data, never authoritative links, login identity, source IDs or membership grants.

normalizeDossierData is deliberately tolerant and lossy; raw import snapshot cannot be reconstructed from its output. Invalid/missing promise IDs and duplicate legacy card IDs need quarantine/provenance, not silent deduplication.
Existing local IDs are dos-* via newLocalId, not necessarily UUIDs despite specification wording 'dossier card UUID aliases'; preserve actual persisted ID strings and namespace.

Two same-name people can currently share summary matches and one messenger suggestion; source identity must remain distinct without treating existing display behavior as canonical relationship evidence.
Imported briefSessionId refers to an existing session whose contents have their own access policy; retaining a link must not publish that session to Company viewers.
A merge with two different notes/promises/brief references must retain both provenances; choosing a scalar winner without retained predecessor fields loses required context.
Changing a local kind chip is not an authorized canonical Contact-to-Company conversion. Kind compatibility and explicit association must be resolved with WP-22.
Cross-private/public merge can leak email through title/snippet/count/search/mention/event/agent caches even if Company detail hides the field; source policy must survive redirects and undo.
Undo that replaces an old graph snapshot can delete later task links and writes; edge revision reconciliation or explicit typed conflict is mandatory.
contracts.ts/commands.ts/repository.ts are shared WP-22 artifacts; nominal newFiles ownership must not cause overwrite or a second CRM authority.
The two proposed migration names and API naming/status differences are integration ambiguities, not authorization to create duplicate tables or transport contracts.

No runtime acceptance is available from this preflight. Source hashes may go stale during root integration; validator must reject changed evidence and lead must re-inspect before applying patch requests.
